text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Classic Twister Ah, the memories I have from playing Twister when I was 16 and drove a red Firebird. Paul, who I wished was my boyfriend was interested in me only as a friend, so the best way I had to get close to him was to invite friends over for a game of Twister. Memories are interesting because I recall exactly what he and I were both wearing -- he in a light blue oxford Gant shirt and me in my self designed and sewn striped wide legged hip-hugger slacks, solid shirt and matching striped vest. I can't tell you who else was there, but we had a full house and we had a blast with my little sister calling our moves and tattling when we were having TOO much fun.

[[ASIN:B00HVTH2MC Classic Twister]] can be played by most ages, provided the bodies are somewhat agile and the individuals are not really shy. The vinyl mat allows for between 2 and 4 people, no more. A game lasts less than 15 minutes usually with the winner being the person who remains on the mat without falling over. A designated person who is not on the mat spins the little plastic on cardboard wheel and those playing place the appropriate limb on a designated spot. For color blind people, your friends will let you know where to put that foot or hand, I guarantee. It is a really fun physical game that stimulates conversation and breaks the ice. I noticed that there are several versions of the game available as of today but cannot tell you what the differences are or why the prices vary. What I can tell you is that this is a really amusing game for all ages, even those who can't actually do the moving but can participate from the peanut gallery.

text_fidelity_a:
Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart This CRAFT-TASTIC 3D STRING ART KIT provides an inexpensive (about $6.25 on Amazon) introduction to the string art craft. It includes a snap-together plastic frame, plenty of colored embroidery floss for string, and reasonably clear instructions. The box says it's for ages 8 and up, which seems about right. (Adult help might be needed to assemble the frame, which requires the pegs to be properly oriented upwards or downwards for everything to snap together tightly.)

There is some artistic creativity involved with this kit, as there are no stringing diagrams to follow. Instead, the instructions say to knot your string to a peg in the frame, and then "wrap the thread from a peg in one (upper) heart to a peg on the other side (the lower heart)." This is simple enough, but it's up to you to choose the pegs so that you get an eye-pleasing criss-crossing of the thread.

Personally, I don't care for the color combinations: bright blue small inside heart, purple edge for the large outside heart, yellow front of large outside heart, pink back of large outside heart. When you're finished with all the stringing, you can set the big heart up on a little plastic stand.

A small child might enjoy this project a lot. However, being an adult, I was bored by the time I'd finished the small blue heart. Because this kit persuaded me that I don't care for the string art craft, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). However, the budget price probably makes it a reasonable purchase if the intent is to keep a small child busy.
text_fidelity_b: Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Mini Neon Marker Maker, 36 Scented Markers, Gift for Kids, Ages 6, 7, 8, 9 This is a great kit. It comes with enough marker-making equipment to make 36 markers, which will last you quite a while. We've played twice with this kit since getting it, and we still have equipment left for making more. The markers themselves are small, and they won't last all that long, but long enough for plenty of use. Everything is very good in terms of quality of components, and ease of making the markers.

One small gripe: making your own colors (i.e. combinations that are not on the helpful color-making sheet they include) is likely going to be a fail. We haven't made a lot of progress in terms of making brown (should be easy, right? - ours looks blue or green), black or even just blends and variations on purple and blue. They tend to look a mess. I guess that's why the color chart is included.

Overall, this is a great kit that will provide hours of entertainment, even for those "too old" to color. It teaches the basics of color mixing and color theory, and is easy for kids to do on their own with minimal supervision. We made a mess too, and it's easy to wipe up!

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces)

GPS Drones, Potensic D50 Quadcopter with Camera Live Video,GPS Return Home, Follow Me, Long Control Range, 5G WiFi Transmission, Great Gift Just a quick note of things you need to know before buying your first drone (and this really is a good choice for a first drone). A drone of this size must be registered with the FAA, and there is a fee associated ($25-$50 for three years -- all prices referenced here are as of the time of this writing). Drones aren't allowed just anywhere, and by "just anywhere" I mean some cities don't let you fly them in your own back yard. They have to be at least 5 miles from an airport, and there are city and state specific regulations. Some entire cities want to be no-fly zones. It's a good idea to check and be sure before you fly.

In New York City, for example, there are five parks in which drones are permitted (none in Manhattan). The best of them, Calvert Vaux Park, requires a membership in the Academy of Model Aeronautics (ModelAviation dot com ) before you can fly there. That organization is recommended by the FAA when you register. Membership will cost from free (for kids) to about $75 a year for the best plan, and that includes liability insurance. Yes, drones can cause damage and if your drone does, you are liable. That's a good resource on where you can and cannot fly and about short term blackouts, such as for public events.

Drones are a learning curve, and classes are very expensive. This particular drone supposedly has a return feature that brings it back to you if the battery is low or if it goes out of range, which is great if you're worried, as I was, about the drone leaving and being lost forever, however the instructions say the remote will beep if the drone is about to go out of range and you need to fly it back or it could fly away and be lost forever. I haven't tested that yet, thankfully, so I'm not sure what to make of it. It has a return button to recall your drone, so long as it's still in range. You can track the GPS of it on the phone as well if that helps and it does have a one key return to call it back. It's a challenge. All drones are. But I find it a little easier than the other few I've had experience with. I'd call it a great first drone for a beginner pilot.

It also has a follow me feature, which basically follows your the controller more or less, which is nice is if you want to go for a run with your drone. Actually, one purpose I had for the drone was to take it on my runs to record my feet, so to watch that I wasn't landing on the side of the foot only to learn I can't have a drone follow me around a random Brooklyn neighborhood. This is great for the extreme sports buff. It can also lock the altitude for easier operation, which is a nice thing. I tend to have problems with drones drifting too high (an issue with my skill, not this drone, but a common issue for new pilots.)

This drone lists as a mini drone, though at 2 pounds it's not like the tiny mini drone that flies only in the house. I'm tempted to try flying this indoors. It seems small enough. It flies for 20 minutes on a charge.
text_fidelity_b: GPS Drones, Potensic D50 Quadcopter with Camera Live Video,GPS Return Home, Follow Me, Long Control Range, 5G WiFi Transmission, Great Gift

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.

VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park 5 stars for the toy itself. 0 stars for the directions - they are awful! The pictures are in blurry black and white, and the wording is confusing. It took me far too long to put together, but I was impressed by the finished product.

First of all - this is big! Look carefully at the specs on this toy to see if it will fit well (or dominate) your play space. The colors and designs are bright and cheerful, which I like. There are a few specific mechanical steps to make this work right with the car, and I worried that it would be too complicated for my 2yo granddaughter. (1) The arm needs to be clicked down into position, (2) you need to wind the car up the ramp (and the crank for that is tricky - if you let go just a little, it slides back to the bottom), then once the car slides down the ramp into the cradle you need to (3) release the arm for the catapult to launch down the second slide. Again - sounds complicated, right? But my granddaughter mastered it in no time! I was surprised and happy about that.

I was also very happy that she played with this over and over. She never seemed to get bored with it. The little car plays music and phrases as it goes along, and even when all the steps didn't go perfectly (ie: the car crashed), my granddaughter was amused. One quick note: some of the joints seem to come apart easily, and since toddlers are a little rough, we needed to keep an eye on this. Still, this will be a great toy that grows with our grandkids!
text_fidelity_b: VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park

I love the big blue traffic cone that fits between the drivers’ cabin and the moveable crane for transport. Tow trucks always set out traffic cones, for safety, when they’re readying a tow. The crane itself is fun because it swings up and down freely.

The building instructions are on the outside of the retail box. The toy takes about 30 seconds for an adult to assemble, as the wheels are already attached to the truck base. When the toy is finished, it makes a terrific truck for general play. The wheels turn freely, and the truck feels solid and satisfying when it’s pushed around.

Inside the box is a printed city street layout. The paper is very thin, so this won’t last long unless it’s glued to some sort of heavier backing. However the street layout fits the assembled tow truck, and is a nice detail.

Note that this is a LEGO duplo model, intended for very young children. The pieces are much larger than standard LEGO pieces. They are compatible with other duplo building sets, but NOT with standard LEGO elements.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces)

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

text_fidelity_a:
Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition Werewolf is not usually a "game night" game that you play with a group of friends. I've always used it in classroom settings, or with larger groups, usually upwards of 10 people, where this game really shines. Ultimately, Werewolf is a deduction game in which most players are Villagers, unwittingly being killed or eliminated by a sect of Werewolf players. Using very limited clues and knowledge, it's up to the Villagers to unmask the Werewolves and eliminate them from the game before they themselves are eaten.

The only real issue that I have with Werewolf is that there is player elimination, although since Werewolf is not a particularly long game, it's usually OK, and bystanders often have as much fun as the players.

There are plenty of versions of this game available out there, but I think that Bezier's "Ultimate" is certainly the way to go. The bits are durable and well made, and there are enough cards to play an 80 person game. That said, there is less content in here as compared to the "Revised Edition" that came out a few years ago. I still think that this is the box to get, however, as the roles and unique playing styles presented in the "Revised" box are more complicated, and not really in line with the casual spirit of the game. I think they certainly provide more variety, but at the expense of complicating the players and making it far more difficult for the moderator. As it's impossible to answer questions mid-game, it's best to leave the complicated roles to a different genre of game.

A 5-Star Product for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition

My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike [[VIDEOID:4ac7ba54c290a47a623bdcdbf7740f53]] This is an excellent My Little Pony doll and puppy. At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form
-Twilight Sparkle can't stand on her own, but this is typical for dolls like this
text_fidelity_b: My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike

Tenergy TB6-B Balance Charger Discharger 1S-6S Digital Battery Pack Charger for NiMH/NiCD/Li-PO/Li-Fe Packs LCD Hobby Battery Charger w/ Tamiya/JST/EC3/HiTec/Deans Connectors + Power Supply 01435 This unit comes with almost everything you need to --

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.

The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink

--------------------------
This was adult owned and taken care of. Mainly used for display, and sparingly demo'ed in the 6 months that I've owned it. I hadn't turned it on for a long while, probably several months. I decided to test it out again, and it wouldn't turn on. I've charged it for over 5 hours. There is a red light to indicate it's charging, but still won't turn on. No longevity for this item. Reducing review to 1-star.

Original Review:
------------------
Very fun light saber! Has a good heft to it and feels high quality. The handle is some sort of aluminum or metal. This looks much better than those plasticky toys. But as usual, with all these sabers on the market, the worst looking part is the the plastic tube. Our tech isn't there yet, but hopefully one day, we can get rid of that plastic tube and have a real solid light beam out! In any case, here are the controls:

-Single click button once to turn on.
-Single click button again to hear effect.
-While it's on, Double click for a blasting sound which the manual calls "lockup mode." It will stay at this sound until you Double Click again to get out of it.
-While it's on, triple click to change colors (this is finicky though)
-Press & hold button to turn off.
-To change the sound "theme," while it's off, hold the button, you will hear a sound theme. Hold the button again to hear the next sound theme, hold it again to hear the next, etc. There is a total of 4 themes, one of which is actually mute.
-To use any of these themes, once you like what you hear, just single click the button to turn on and play. Remember clicking once turns it on, but holding the button would cause it to cycle through the themes. But once on, to get back to cycling through the themes, you need to press & hold to turn off first, then press & hold to cycle through the themes.

My kids have a few sabers from the out of business toy store. This one belongs to daddy. LOL! I'm knocking 1 star for the finicky controls and instructions that were a little hard to figure out. 4 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

*The attached photos are of the ant farm on day 3.

LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces) As a child, I loved pop-up books, so of course I love all of the LEGO pop-up book building kits. The first one (see [[ASIN:B07GYB8D34 LEGO Pop-Up Book]] originated as a fan model submitted to the LEGO Ideas fan-voting site (if you want to participate, just google for LEGO Ideas). This DISNEY MULAN’S STORYBOOK ADVENTURES 43174 BUILDING KIT (New 2020 (124 Pieces)) is a smaller, simpler version of the original pop-up book, but it’s still a lot of fun.

The basic pop-up feature is the arched bridge that goes from the center--the book’s stationary spine, where Mulan’s buildings are--to the little “tea service” island in the left half of the book. The bridge goes up and down on a LEGO hinge, and snaps into place when the book is completely open.

There are LEGO studs strategically placed around the open book, so that the three dolls, Mulan’s pony, and Mulan’s cricket cage can all be firmly attached at once. This way, they don’t rattle around loose (or get lost) when the book is closed to be put away. When the book is open for play, the dolls fit on the bridge, under the arches, and can stand anywhere on the book surface.

The assembly instructions are reasonably easy to follow--just look closely at the pictures. I had to take my book covers apart and reassemble them because I got the left (blue water) and right (white land) sides switched, so that the water was on the wrong side when the book was opened.

There are quite a few stickers, but only a few that need to be carefully placed on LEGO elements. The instructions aren’t terribly clear on where to place the stickers that go onto the book’s interior surfaces (e.g., the swimming Koi fish, the lily pads, Mulan’s bed roll, the campfire, the cooking supplies). You can consult the box photos, or even the photos in the online LEGO Shop, if you want extra guidance for these.

One of my favorite features is the two little tassels or bells that swing from Mulan’s temple-like building. I don’t know whether this is an entirely new LEGO element, or whether it has appeared in other sets, but it was new to me. There are enough LEGO pieces in the set to make the book interesting to assemble; and the book is fun to play with after it’s built.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces)

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
